cards.explanation: The reason the song gives is that He is good. It says, "Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good." The reason comes in the same breath as the call, friends. I once made a whole speech before telling a baker what the dough was for, so I respect a song that gets right to it.
The answer is forever. The line says, "His loving devotion endures forever." Not a long time, not a really long time. Forever, friends. And the song says it again and again, after every single line.
The answer is False. Verse 4 says, "He alone does great wonders." There's no helper list and no assistants mentioned, friends. When the song says alone, it means alone.

The answer is True. The song says, "By His insight He made the heavens." Every star up there came from insight, friends, not from a lucky accident. And all of it is followed by that same line about His loving devotion.

The answer is True. The song says, "He spread out the earth upon the waters." From the heavens it comes down to the ground under our feet, friends. The refrain about His loving devotion follows right behind it.

The answers are day and night. The song says He made "…the sun to rule the day…" The sun has the day shift, friends. It's a very big job, and the sun never calls in sick. Then the song says "…the moon and stars to govern the night." So the moon and stars take the night, and the bakery is under the same sky.

The answer is False. Verse 12 says He brought Israel out "…with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm." That's a power on display, friends, not a sneaking out the back door. I would have tripped over a rolling pin trying to be quiet.

The answer is that He leads them through the middle. The song says He "…led Israel through the midst…" The sea is divided in two, friends, and Israel goes right through the middle of it. The song doesn't say it was an easy walk, only that He led them.

The answer is that they are swept into the sea. The song says He "…swept Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea." Pharaoh was Egypt's king. Israel went through the divided sea, friends, and Pharaoh and his army ended up in it. It's a serious moment, so I'll just let the verse speak.

The answer is land. The song says He "…gave their land as an inheritance…" The kings were Sihon and Og, friends, and their land became a heritage for His servant Israel. Think of it as a gift handed down.

The answer is our enemies. The song says He "…freed us from our enemies." First He remembered us in our low estate, friends, and then He freed us. And the refrain about His loving devotion comes right after.
The answer is False. The song says, "He gives food to every creature." Every creature, friends, not just some. Even the crumb collectors under my counter are in that group.

The answer is True. The song opens with "Give thanks to the LORD…" and it closes with "Give thanks to the God of heaven!" It ends where it began, friends. And both times, His loving devotion endures forever.
